- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak or adjust downward by 1–3 points.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) mid-horizon, model frequently fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5 points per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0 point.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.5), model often underestimates; add 0.2–0.8 point bias upward.
- Lagged sentiment (e.g., 3–5 days prior) strongly influences direction: if sentiment was positive 3+ days ago, model may be overconfident; adjust downward 0.3–0.7 points.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid “early peak” bias — if model peaks early (e.g., day 1–5), reduce by 0.5–1.0 point to align with true trend.
